title.zh: 卷90 逸士:眭誇 馮亮 李謐 鄭修
title.en: Volume 90: Retired Officals - Sui Kua, Feng Liang, Li Mi, Zheng Xiu
title.raw: 卷90 逸士:眭誇 馮亮 李謐 鄭修 Volume 90: Retired Officals - Sui Kua, Feng Liang, Li Mi, Zheng Xiu

sentences.zh: 眭夸 馮亮 李謐 鄭脩

translations.literal: Sui Kua, Feng Liang, Li Mi, Zheng Xiu
translations.idiomatic: Sui Kua, Feng Liang, Li Mi, and Zheng Xiu

sentences.zh: 蓋兼濟獨善，顯晦之殊，其事不同，由來久矣。

translations.literal: For benefiting all and perfecting oneself alone, the distinction between manifest and hidden—their affairs differ; this has been so for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The paths of serving the common good and cultivating oneself in solitude, of public renown and private withdrawal—these have never been the same, and the difference is ancient.

sentences.zh: 昔夷齊獲全於周武，華矞不容於太公，何哉？

translations.literal: In the past Boyi and Shuqi were preserved whole under King Wu of Zhou, while Hua Yu was not tolerated by Duke Tai of Qi—why?
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Boyi and Shuqi were spared by King Wu of Zhou, yet Hua Yu found no place with Duke Tai of Qi—why was this?

sentences.zh: 求其心者，許以激貪之用；

translations.literal: Those who seek their hearts approve them for stirring the greedy to reform;
translations.idiomatic: Those who probe their motives credit them with the power to rouse the grasping from corruption;

sentences.zh: 督其迹者，以為束教之風。

translations.literal: Those who scrutinize their conduct regard them as a discipline for instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Those who judge them by their deeds take them as a model for restraining custom.

sentences.zh: 而肥遁不反，代有人矣。

translations.literal: Yet those who retire deep into seclusion and do not return—every age has had such men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet men who withdraw far into reclusion and never return back—each generation has produced them.

sentences.zh: 夷情得喪，忘懷累有。

translations.literal: Detached from worldly emotion, gain and loss forgotten—such cases abound.
translations.idiomatic: Indifferent to worldly passion, heedless of gain and loss—examples are many.

sentences.zh: 比夫邁德弘道，匡俗庇民，可得而小，不可得而忽也。

translations.literal: Compared with advancing virtue and spreading the Way, correcting custom and sheltering the people, they may be slighted but cannot be disregarded.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against those who advance virtue, broaden the Way, reform society, and shelter the people, such men may seem small in scale, yet they cannot be dismissed lightly.

sentences.zh: 自叔世澆浮，淳風殆盡，錐刀之末，競入成羣，而能冥心物表，介然離俗，望古獨適，求友千齡，亦異人矣。

translations.literal: Since the decadent age, pure custom has nearly perished; at the tip of a knife's edge men rush in crowds—yet those who can darken their minds beyond things, stand apart from the vulgar, look to antiquity alone for their path, and seek friends across a thousand years are also extraordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: From the fallen age onward, honest manners have all but vanished; men scramble over the smallest profit. Yet those who can fix their minds beyond the world of things, stand aloof from vulgar life, take antiquity alone as their measure, and seek kindred spirits across a thousand years are rare beings indeed.

sentences.zh: 何必御霞乘雲而追日月，窮極天地，始為超遠哉。

translations.literal: Why must one ride mist and mount clouds to chase sun and moon, exhaust heaven and earth, before being deemed transcendent?
translations.idiomatic: Why must one ride the clouds and pursue the sun and moon, traversing heaven and earth to the limit, before being called truly remote from the world?

sentences.zh: 今錄眭夸等為逸士傳。

translations.literal: Now Sui Kua and the others are recorded in a Biography of Reclusive Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Here Sui Kua and the others are entered in a Biography of Reclusive Scholars.

sentences.zh: 眭夸，一名昶，趙郡高邑人也。

translations.literal: Sui Kua, also named Chang, was a native of Gaoyi in Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Kua, also called Chang, came from Gaoyi in Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖邁，晉東海王越軍謀掾，後沒石勒為徐州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mai was a military adviser to Prince of Donghai Yue of Jin; later, having fallen to Shi Le, he served as Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mai had been a military adviser to Jin's Prince of Donghai, Yue; after capture by Shi Le he became Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父邃，字懷道，慕容寶中書令。

translations.literal: His father Sui, styled Huaidao, was Secretariat Director under Murong Bao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sui, styled Huaidao, served Murong Bao as Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 夸少有大度，不拘小節，耽志書傳，未曾以世務經心。

translations.literal: Kua from youth had great breadth of spirit, did not bind himself to petty rules, devoted himself to books and records, and never once turned his mind to worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Kua was broad-minded from youth, careless of small proprieties, absorbed in books and histories, and never gave worldly business a thought.

sentences.zh: 好飲酒，浩然物表。

translations.literal: He loved wine and dwelt far beyond things with an easy grandeur.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and lived with an unworldly ease beyond the common round.

sentences.zh: 年二十遭父喪，鬚鬢致白，每一悲哭，聞者為之流涕。

translations.literal: At twenty he suffered his father's death; his beard and hair turned white; each time he wept in grief, listeners were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he lost his father; his beard and hair turned white, and each time he mourned aloud those who heard him wept.

sentences.zh: 高尚不仕，寄情丘壑。

translations.literal: Noble-minded, he would not take office and poured his feelings into hills and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty in spirit, he refused office and gave his heart to mountain and stream.

sentences.zh: 同郡李順願與之交，夸拒而不許。

translations.literal: Li Shun of the same commandery wished to befriend him, but Kua refused and would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shun of his commandery wished to associate with him; Kua declined.

sentences.zh: 邦國少長莫不憚之。

translations.literal: Young and old throughout the state all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Young and old in the realm alike stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 少與崔浩為莫逆之交。

translations.literal: In youth he was sworn friends with Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he and Cui Hao were inseparable friends.

sentences.zh: 浩為司徒，奏徵為其中郎，辭疾不赴。

translations.literal: When Hao became Minister of Works, he memorialized to summon Kua as Palace Gentleman, but Kua pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao became Minister of Works he recommended Kua as Palace Gentleman; Kua pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 州郡逼遣，不得已，入京都。

translations.literal: The province and commandery pressed him to go; unable to refuse further, he entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial and commandery authorities pressed him until, with no choice left, he entered the capital.

sentences.zh: 與浩相見，延留數日，惟飲酒談敍平生，不及世利。

translations.literal: Meeting Hao, he stayed several days, drinking only and talking over their lives, never touching worldly profit.
translations.idiomatic: On meeting Hao he lingered several days, drinking and recalling their past alone, never speaking of worldly gain.

sentences.zh: 浩每欲論屈之，竟不能發言。

translations.literal: Hao each time wished to argue and bend him to his will, yet in the end could not bring himself to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Hao meant each time to argue him into compliance, yet could never bring himself to begin.

sentences.zh: 其見敬憚如此。

translations.literal: Such was the respect and awe in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the deference he inspired.

sentences.zh: 浩後遂投詔書於夸懷，亦不開口。

translations.literal: Later Hao tossed the imperial edict into Kua's bosom; Kua still would not open his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Hao then thrust the imperial edict into Kua's robe; Kua still would not speak.

sentences.zh: 夸曰：「桃簡，卿已為司徒，何足以此勞國士也。

translations.literal: Kua said: "Taojian, you are already Minister of Works—why trouble a man of the realm with this?
translations.idiomatic: Kua said, "Taojian, you are already Minister of Works—what need is there to weary a man of the realm with such a thing?

sentences.zh: 吾便於此將別。」

translations.literal: I shall take my leave here."
translations.idiomatic: I shall bid farewell here."

sentences.zh: 桃簡，浩小名也。

translations.literal: Taojian was Hao's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Taojian was Hao's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 浩慮夸即還。

translations.literal: Hao feared Kua would leave at once.
translations.idiomatic: Hao feared Kua would return home at once.

sentences.zh: 時乘一騾，更無兼騎，浩乃以夸騾內之廐中，冀相維縶。

translations.literal: At the time he rode a single mule with no spare mount; Hao therefore stabled Kua's mule in his own stable, hoping to detain him.
translations.idiomatic: Kua had come on a single mule with no second mount; Hao stabled the mule in his own stable, hoping to hold him back.

sentences.zh: 夸遂託鄉人輸租者，謬為御車，乃得出關。

translations.literal: Kua then entrusted himself to a fellow townsman who delivered rent grain, falsely posing as the driver, and thus got out through the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Kua then joined a townsman delivering rent grain, passed himself off as the driver, and so slipped through the pass.

sentences.zh: 浩知而歎曰：「眭夸獨行士，本不應以小職辱之。

translations.literal: When Hao learned of it he sighed: "Sui Kua is a man who walks alone; he should not have been insulted with a petty post.
translations.idiomatic: Learning this, Hao sighed: "Sui Kua is a man who walks alone; he should never have been pressed with a petty office.

sentences.zh: 又使其人仗策復路，吾當何辭以謝也。」

translations.literal: And now I have sent him off on foot with a staff down the road—what words can I offer in apology?"
translations.idiomatic: And I have sent him walking home with a staff—what apology can I possibly make?"

sentences.zh: 時朝法甚峻，夸既私還，將有私歸之咎。

translations.literal: Court law was then very strict; since Kua had returned without permission, he would face the charge of unauthorized departure."
translations.idiomatic: Court law was severe; Kua's unauthorized return would have brought punishment for leaving without leave.

sentences.zh: 浩仍相左右，始得無坐。

translations.literal: Hao still stood by him on both sides until at last he escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Hao continued to shield him until he escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 經年，送夸本騾，兼遺以所乘馬，為書謝之。

translations.literal: After a year he sent back Kua's mule and also gave him the horse he himself had ridden, with a letter of apology.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he returned Kua's mule, sent the horse he had ridden, and wrote to apologize.

sentences.zh: 夸更不受其騾馬，亦不復書。

translations.literal: Kua again would not accept mule or horse and wrote no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Kua again refused mule and horse and sent no letter in return.

sentences.zh: 及浩誅，為之素服，受鄉人弔唁，經一時乃止。

translations.literal: When Hao was executed, Kua wore unbleached mourning, accepted condolences from fellow townsfolk, and only after a time stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was put to death, Kua wore plain mourning, received condolences from his neighbors, and only after a time laid it aside.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「崔公既死，誰能更容眭夸！」

translations.literal: He sighed: "Now that Lord Cui is dead, who can still tolerate Sui Kua!"
translations.idiomatic: He sighed, "Lord Cui is dead—who will shelter Sui Kua now?"

sentences.zh: 遂作朋友篇，辭義為時人所稱。

translations.literal: He then composed an essay On Friendship, whose wording was praised by men of the time."
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote an essay On Friendship, praised in his day for its force.

sentences.zh: 婦父鉅鹿魏攀，當時名達之士。

translations.literal: His wife's father Wei Pan of Julu was a man of renown in that age.
translations.idiomatic: His father-in-law Wei Pan of Julu was a celebrated man of the time.

sentences.zh: 未嘗備壻之禮，情同朋好。

translations.literal: He never performed the rites due a son-in-law; their feeling was like that between friends.
translations.idiomatic: He never observed son-in-law proprieties; they were friends in spirit.

sentences.zh: 或人謂夸曰：「吾聞有大才者必居貴仕，子何獨在桑榆乎？」

translations.literal: Someone said to Kua: "I have heard that men of great talent must hold lofty office—why do you alone linger at sunset?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Kua, "Men of great talent, I am told, must hold high office—why do you alone linger in life's evening?"

sentences.zh: 遂著知命論以釋之。

translations.literal: He thereupon wrote an essay On Accepting Fate to explain."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote an essay On Accepting Fate to answer them.

sentences.zh: 年七十五卒。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 葬日，赴會者如市。

translations.literal: On the day of burial, those who came were like a market crowd.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his burial mourners thronged like a market.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons.

sentences.zh: 馮亮，字靈通，南陽人，蕭衍平北將軍蔡道恭之甥也。

translations.literal: Feng Liang, styled Lingtong, was a man of Nanyang, nephew of Cai Daogong, General Who Pacifies the North under Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Liang, styled Lingtong, came from Nanyang; he was nephew to Xiao Yan's General Who Pacifies the North, Cai Daogong.

sentences.zh: 少博覽諸書，又篤好佛理。

translations.literal: In youth he read widely among books and was also deeply devoted to Buddhist doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he read widely and was deeply devoted to Buddhist teaching.

sentences.zh: 隨道恭至義陽，會中山王英平義陽而獲焉。

translations.literal: He followed Daogong to Yiyang; when Prince of Zhongshan Ying pacified Yiyang he was taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Daogong to Yiyang; when Prince of Zhongshan Ying took the city, Liang was captured.

sentences.zh: 英素聞其名，以禮待接。

translations.literal: Ying had long heard his name and received him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had long known his reputation and treated him with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 亮性清淨，至洛，隱居崧高，感英之德，以時展勤。

translations.literal: Liang's nature was pure and still; reaching Luoyang he retired to Mount Song, moved by Ying's kindness, and from time to time paid his respects.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was pure in temperament; reaching Luoyang he withdrew to Mount Song, grateful for Ying's kindness, and visited him from time to time.

sentences.zh: 及英亡，亮奔赴，盡其哀慟。

translations.literal: When Ying died, Liang hurried to the funeral and gave full vent to grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying died, Liang rushed to the mourning and grieved to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘗召以為羽林監，領中書舍人，將令侍講十地諸經，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong once summoned him as Captain of the Feathered Forest and concurrently Palace Scribe, intending to have him lecture on the Ten Grounds sutras, but he firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong summoned him as Captain of the Feathered Forest with concurrent duty as Palace Scribe, intending to have him expound the Ten Grounds sutras; he firmly refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 又欲使衣幘入見，亮苦求以幅巾就朝，遂不強逼。

translations.literal: They also wished him to enter audience wearing a kerchiefed cap; Liang begged hard to attend court in a plain headcloth, and they did not force him.
translations.idiomatic: The court wished him to appear in formal cap; Liang begged to attend in a plain headcloth, and they did not press him.

sentences.zh: 還山數年，與僧徒禮誦為業，蔬食飲水，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Returning to the mountains for several years, he made ritual chanting with monks his occupation, ate vegetables and drank water, and had the will to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the hills for years he chanted sutras with monks, lived on vegetables and water, and meant to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 會逆人王敞事發，連山中沙門，而亮被執赴尚書省，十餘日，詔特免雪。

translations.literal: When the rebel Wang Chang's affair broke out, mountain monks were implicated; Liang was seized and taken to the Ministry of State, but after more than ten days an edict specially cleared him.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Wang Chang's plot surfaced, mountain monks were swept up; Liang was seized and held at the Ministry of State, then specially pardoned after ten-odd days.

sentences.zh: 亮不敢還山，遂寓居景明寺。

translations.literal: Liang dared not return to the mountains and therefore lodged at Jingming Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He dared not return to the hills and lodged at Jingming Temple.

sentences.zh: 敕給衣食及其從者數人。

translations.literal: An edict supplied food and clothing for him and several attendants.
translations.idiomatic: An edict provided food, clothing, and several attendants.

sentences.zh: 後思其舊居，復還山室。

translations.literal: Later, thinking of his old dwelling, he returned to his mountain cell.
translations.idiomatic: Later, longing for his old retreat, he went back to his mountain cell.

sentences.zh: 亮既雅愛山水，又兼巧思，結架巖林，甚得栖游之適，頗以此聞。

translations.literal: Liang both loved landscape in refined taste and was also skilled in design; he built structures among cliffs and woods with great fitness for dwelling and roaming, and became known for this.
translations.idiomatic: Liang loved landscape and had a gift for design; his cliff and forest structures suited dwelling and wandering so well that fame spread.

sentences.zh: 世宗給其工力，[2]令與沙門統僧暹、河南尹甄琛等，周視崧高形勝之處，遂造閑居佛寺。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong gave him laborers and ordered him, with the Buddhist overseer Sengxian, Henan Intendant Zhen Chen, and others, to survey Mount Song's commanding sites and there build a reclusive Buddhist temple.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him workmen and ordered him, with the Buddhist overseer Sengxian, Henan Intendant Zhen Chen, and others, to tour Mount Song's finest sites and build a reclusive temple.

sentences.zh: 林泉既奇，營製又美，曲盡山居之妙。

translations.literal: The woods and springs were already marvelous, the construction also beautiful, fully expressing the subtlety of mountain dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Wood and spring were wondrous, the construction exquisite—mountain life at its finest.

sentences.zh: 亮時出京師。

translations.literal: Liang would sometimes come out to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: From time to time Liang came down to the capital.

sentences.zh: 延昌二年冬，因遇篤疾，世宗敕以馬輿送令還山，居崧高道場寺。

translations.literal: In winter of the second year of Yanchang, falling gravely ill, Emperor Shizong ordered a palanquin to convey him back to the mountains; he dwelt at the Daochang Temple on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of Yanchang year 2, gravely ill, he was sent by imperial palanquin to Mount Song's Daochang Temple.

sentences.zh: 數日而卒。

translations.literal: Within several days he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died within days.

sentences.zh: 詔贈帛二百匹，以供凶事。

translations.literal: An edict granted two hundred bolts of silk for funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted two hundred bolts of silk for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 遺誡兄子綜，斂以衣㡊，左手持板，右手執孝經一卷，置尸盤石上，去人數里外。

translations.literal: He left instructions to his nephew Zong: wrap the body in hemp garments; left hand hold a tablet, right hand grasp one roll of the Classic of Filial Piety; place the corpse on a flat stone several li from men.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed his nephew Zong: enshroud him in hemp, left hand on a tablet, right hand holding one roll of the Classic of Filial Piety; lay the body on a stone slab miles from any dwelling.

sentences.zh: 積十餘日，乃焚於山。

translations.literal: After more than ten days they burned him on the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: After ten-odd days they burned him on the mountain.

sentences.zh: 以灰燼處，起佛塔經藏。

translations.literal: At the place of ashes they raised a stupa and sutra repository.
translations.idiomatic: At the ashes they raised a stupa and sutra repository.

sentences.zh: 初，亮以盛冬喪，時連日驟雪，窮山荒澗，鳥獸飢窘，僵尸山野，無所防護。

translations.literal: At first, because Liang died in deep winter when snow fell day after day, in desolate mountains and wild ravines birds and beasts were famished; the corpse lay in the open hills with no protection.
translations.idiomatic: Liang died in deep winter amid days of driving snow; in desolate hills birds and beasts starved, and his corpse lay unguarded in the wild.

sentences.zh: 時壽春道人惠需，每旦往看其屍，拂去塵霰。

translations.literal: The Shouchun monk Huixu each dawn went to view the corpse and brushed away dust and hail.
translations.idiomatic: The Shouchun monk Huixu came each dawn to brush dust and hail from the body.

sentences.zh: 禽蟲之迹，交橫左右，而初無侵毀，衣服如本，惟風吹㡊巾。

translations.literal: Tracks of birds and insects crossed left and right, yet at first there was no harm; the clothes were as before, only the wind stirred the hemp headcloth.
translations.idiomatic: Bird and insect tracks crossed the body, yet nothing harmed it; the clothes were untouched save that wind stirred the hemp cloth.

sentences.zh: 又以亮識舊南方法師信大栗十枚，言期之將來十地果報，開亮手以置把中。

translations.literal: He also placed ten large chestnuts from the southern monk Xin, whom Liang had known, saying they betokened future reward of the Ten Grounds; he opened Liang's hand and set them in his grasp.
translations.idiomatic: He placed ten large chestnuts from the southern monk Xin, an old acquaintance of Liang's, saying they foretold Ten Grounds reward, and laid them in Liang's open hand.

sentences.zh: 經宿，乃為蟲鳥盜食，皮殼在地，而亦不傷肌體。

translations.literal: After a night they were stolen and eaten by insects and birds; the shells lay on the ground yet the flesh was unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: Overnight birds and insects ate the chestnuts; shells littered the ground, yet Liang's flesh was unharmed.

sentences.zh: 焚燎之日，有素霧蓊鬱，迴繞其傍，自地屬天，彌朝不絕。

translations.literal: On the day of burning, pale mist rose dense and circled beside him from earth to heaven, unbroken through the morning.
translations.idiomatic: On the cremation day pale mist rose thick about him from earth to sky and lingered all morning.

sentences.zh: 山中道俗營助者百餘人，莫不異焉。

translations.literal: More than a hundred monks and layfolk who assisted were all astonished.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred-odd monks and lay helpers were all astonished.

sentences.zh: 李謐，字永和，趙郡人，[3]相州刺史安世之子。

translations.literal: Li Mi, styled Yonghe, was a man of Zhao commandery, son of Anshi, Inspector of Xiang province.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi, styled Yonghe, came from Zhao commandery; he was son of Anshi, Inspector of Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 少好學，博通諸經，周覽百氏。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning, mastered the classics, and surveyed the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning, mastered the classics, and ranged through the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 初師事小學博士孔璠。

translations.literal: At first he studied under the Erudite of Elementary Learning Kong Fan.
translations.idiomatic: At first he studied under the Erudite of Elementary Learning, Kong Fan.

sentences.zh: 數年後，璠還就謐請業。

translations.literal: Several years later Fan in turn came to Mi to request instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Years later Fan himself came to Mi to seek instruction.

sentences.zh: 同門生為之語曰：「青成藍，藍謝青，師何常，在明經。」

translations.literal: Fellow students made a saying of it: "Green makes blue, blue leaves green—what constancy has a teacher when clarity rests in the bright classic?"
translations.idiomatic: His fellows said, "Green outdoes blue, then blue surpasses green—what fixity has the teacher when mastery lies in the enlightened classic?"

sentences.zh: 謐以公子徵拜著作佐郎，辭以授弟郁，詔許之。

translations.literal: Mi was summoned as Assistant Editor on account of his noble birth but declined, transferring the post to his younger brother Yu; the edict permitted it."
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as Assistant Editor on account of his birth rank, Mi declined and gave the post to his younger brother Yu; the throne assented.

sentences.zh: 州再舉秀才，公府二辟，並不就。

translations.literal: The province twice nominated him as Outstanding Talent; the government offices twice summoned him—he accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: Twice nominated as Outstanding Talent by his province, twice summoned by the government—he refused both.

sentences.zh: 惟以琴書為業，有絕世之心。

translations.literal: He took only zither and books as his occupation and had a mind to leave the world behind.
translations.idiomatic: He lived only for zither and books and meant to withdraw from the world.

sentences.zh: 覽考工記、大戴禮盛德篇，以明堂之制不同，遂著明堂制度論曰：

translations.literal: Reading the Records of the Craftsman and the "Accomplished Virtue" chapter of the Elder Dai's Rites, and finding the Mingtang regulations differ, he therefore wrote an essay On the Mingtang System, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Reading the Records of the Craftsman and the "Accomplished Virtue" chapter of Elder Dai's Rites, and finding the Mingtang regulations at odds, he wrote an essay On the Mingtang System, which says:

sentences.zh: 余謂論事辨物，當取正於經典之真文；

translations.literal: I hold that in discussing affairs and distinguishing things one should take correctness from the authentic text of the classics;
translations.idiomatic: I hold that in discussing affairs and distinguishing things one must take one's standard from the authentic text of the classics;

sentences.zh: 援證定疑，必有驗於周孔之遺訓。

translations.literal: in citing evidence to settle doubt there must be verification in the surviving teachings of Zhou and Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: to settle doubt by evidence one must find confirmation in what Zhou and Confucius handed down.

sentences.zh: 然後可以稱準的矣。

translations.literal: Only then may one be said to have a true measure.
translations.idiomatic: Only then can one claim a true standard.

sentences.zh: 今禮文殘缺，聖言靡存，明堂之制，誰使正之。

translations.literal: Now the ritual texts are defective, the sage's words scarcely survive, and who can set right the Mingtang regulations?
translations.idiomatic: Today the ritual texts are broken, the sage's words nearly gone—who can correct the Mingtang regulations?

sentences.zh: 是以後人紛糾，競興異論，五九之說，各信其習。

translations.literal: Hence later men are tangled in dispute, each school trusting its own habit, competing to raise strange theories—the five-nine theories each believing its custom.
translations.idiomatic: Hence later scholars tangle in dispute, each trusting habit, the theories of five chambers and nine chambers alike clinging to custom.

sentences.zh: 是非無準，得失相半。

translations.literal: Right and wrong have no standard; gain and loss are half and half.
translations.idiomatic: There is no standard for right and wrong; gain and loss divide evenly.

sentences.zh: 故歷代紛紜，靡所取正。

translations.literal: Therefore through the ages confusion has reigned with nothing to take as correct.
translations.idiomatic: Through the ages confusion has ruled, with nothing to adopt as correct.

sentences.zh: 乃使裴頠云：「今羣儒紛糾，互相掎摭，就令其象可得而圖，其所以居用之禮莫能通也，為設虛器耳。

translations.literal: This led Pei Wei to say: "Now the Confucians are tangled, each pulling down the other; even if one could diagram their forms, the rites by which they would be used cannot be made to cohere—it is setting up empty vessels.
translations.idiomatic: This led Pei Wei to say, "Confucians now tangle in dispute, each pulling the other down; even if their forms could be drawn, the rites of use cannot be made coherent—it is empty vessels.

sentences.zh: 況漢氏所作，四維之个，復不能令各處其辰。

translations.literal: Moreover what the Han made—the four corner posts—again could not be made each to occupy its season.
translations.idiomatic: What the Han dynasty built, with its four corner posts, could not even place each in its proper season.

sentences.zh: 愚以為尊祖配天，其儀明著；

translations.literal: I deem honoring the ancestor and matching Heaven—their rites are clear and plain;
translations.idiomatic: Honoring the ancestor and matching Heaven—these rites are clear;

sentences.zh: 廟宇之制，理據未分。

translations.literal: the regulations for temples and halls—their principles are undivided.
translations.idiomatic: temple and hall regulations—their principles remain unsettled.

sentences.zh: 直可為殿屋以崇嚴父之祀，其餘雜碎一皆除之。」

translations.literal: One need only build a hall to exalt the father's sacrifice; all other miscellaneous details should be removed."
translations.idiomatic: Build only a hall to dignify the father's sacrifice; cut away every other miscellaneous detail."

sentences.zh: 斯豈不以羣儒舛互，並乖其實，據義求衷，莫適可從哉？

translations.literal: Is this not because the Confucians contradict one another, all departing from fact, and when one seeks the mean by principle, nothing can be followed?"
translations.idiomatic: Is it not because the Confucians contradict one another, all missing the truth, so that when one seeks the mean by principle, nothing can be adopted?

sentences.zh: 但恨典文殘滅，求之靡據而已矣。

translations.literal: One only regrets that the canonical texts are destroyed and that nothing can be found to serve as evidence.
translations.idiomatic: One can only regret that the canonical texts are ruined and that no firm evidence remains.

sentences.zh: 乃復遂去室牖諸制。

translations.literal: He then went on to remove the regulations for chambers, doors, and windows.
translations.idiomatic: He then cast aside the regulations for chambers, doors, and windows as well.

sentences.zh: 施之於教，未知其所隆政；

translations.literal: Applied to instruction, it is unknown what government it would exalt;
translations.idiomatic: Applied to teaching, one cannot tell what government it would dignify;

sentences.zh: 求之於情，未可喻其所以必須。

translations.literal: sought in human feeling, one cannot explain why it must be required.
translations.idiomatic: weighed by human feeling, one cannot explain why it must be required.

sentences.zh: 惜哉言乎！

translations.literal: Alas for such words!
translations.idiomatic: What a pity, such words!

sentences.zh: 仲尼有言曰：「賜也，爾愛其羊，我愛其禮。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: "Ci, you love the sheep; I love the ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Ci, you care for the sheep; I care for the ritual."

sentences.zh: 余以為隆政必須其禮，豈彼一羊哉！

translations.literal: I hold that exalting government must require ritual—how could it be that one sheep!"
translations.idiomatic: I hold that exalting government requires ritual--surely it is not a matter of one sheep alone!

sentences.zh: 推此而論，則聖人之於禮，殷勤而重之，裴頠之於禮，任意而忽之。

translations.literal: Pushing this to discuss it, the sage toward ritual was earnest and weighty, while Pei Wei toward ritual was arbitrary and neglectful.
translations.idiomatic: By this reasoning the sage honored ritual with earnest care, while Pei Wei treated ritual arbitrarily and lightly.

sentences.zh: 是則頠賢於仲尼矣。

translations.literal: In that case Pei would be worthier than Zhongni.
translations.idiomatic: By that logic Pei would surpass Zhongni.

sentences.zh: 以斯觀之，裴氏之子以不達而失禮之旨也。

translations.literal: Viewed thus, the son of the Pei clan failed the aim of ritual through lack of understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Seen this way, Pei's follower missed the point of ritual through incomprehension.

sentences.zh: 余竊不自量，頗有鄙意，據理尋義，以求其真，貴合雅衷，不苟偏信。

translations.literal: I venture without measuring myself to have a humble opinion: seeking truth by principle and meaning, valuing accord with refined intent, not crediting partial belief.
translations.idiomatic: I do not presume on my own measure, yet I have a view: I seek truth by principle, value refined intent, and will not cling to partial belief.

sentences.zh: 乃藉之以禮傳，考之以訓注，博採先賢之言，廣搜通儒之說，量其當否，參其同異，棄其所短，收其所長，推義察圖，以折厥衷。

translations.literal: I therefore rely on the ritual tradition, examine commentaries, broadly gather the words of former worthies and widely search the theories of accomplished Confucians, weigh their right and wrong, compare their agreements and differences, discard what is short, gather what is long, push meaning and inspect diagrams to settle the mean.
translations.idiomatic: I rely on the ritual tradition, test it against commentaries, gather the words of former worthies and search the theories of accomplished scholars, weigh right and wrong, compare agreements and differences, discard the weak, keep the strong, and settle the mean by reasoning and diagram.

sentences.zh: 豈敢必善，聊亦合其言志矣。

translations.literal: I dare not claim it must be good, yet it at least accords with the intent of my words.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not claim perfection, yet it at least matches what I mean to say.

sentences.zh: 凡論明堂之制者雖眾，然校其大略，則二途而已。

translations.literal: Those who discuss the Mingtang regulations are many, yet comparing the general outline, there are only two paths.
translations.idiomatic: Many have discussed the Mingtang regulations, yet in broad outline there are only two schools.

sentences.zh: 言五室者，則據周禮考工之記以為本，是康成之徒所執；

translations.literal: Those who speak of five chambers take the "Artificers" record in the Zhou Rites as foundation—this is what the followers of Zheng Xuan hold;
translations.idiomatic: The five-chamber school takes the Zhou Rites "Artificers" record as its foundation—the party of Zheng Xuan;

sentences.zh: 言九室者，則案大戴盛德之篇以為源，是伯喈之倫所持。

translations.literal: those who speak of nine chambers take the "Accomplished Virtue" chapter of Elder Dai as source—this is what the party of Cai Yong holds.
translations.idiomatic: the nine-chamber school takes Elder Dai's "Accomplished Virtue" chapter as its source—the party of Cai Yong.

sentences.zh: 此之二書，雖非聖言，然是先賢之中博見洽通者也。

translations.literal: These two books, though not sage words, are among the former worthies the most broadly seen and thoroughly penetrated.
translations.idiomatic: Neither book is the sage's own words, yet both belong to the most learned and penetrating of the former worthies.

sentences.zh: 但各記所聞，未能全正，可謂既盡美矣，未盡善也。

translations.literal: Yet each recorded what he heard and could not wholly correct it—one may say they reached beauty but not goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Each recorded what he heard and could not wholly set it right—they reached beauty, perhaps, but not full goodness.

sentences.zh: 而先儒不能考其當否，便各是所習，卒相非毀，豈達士之確論哉？

translations.literal: Former Confucians could not examine their right and wrong and each affirmed what he had learned, ending by mutually slandering—how is this the sure discourse of an accomplished man?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Confucians never tested their right and wrong; each clung to his own training and ended in mutual attack—this is hardly the sure judgment of a true scholar.

sentences.zh: 小戴氏傳禮事四十九篇，號曰禮記，雖未能全當，然多得其衷，方之前賢，亦無愧矣。

translations.literal: Younger Dai transmitted forty-nine chapters of ritual affairs, called the Record of Rites; though not wholly correct, he mostly hit the center, and compared with earlier worthies he need not be ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Younger Dai transmitted forty-nine ritual chapters called the Record of Rites; though not wholly correct, he mostly hit the mark and need not blush before earlier worthies.

sentences.zh: 而月令、玉藻、明堂三篇，頗有明堂之義，余故採掇二家，參之月令，以為明堂五室，古今通則。

translations.literal: The chapters "Monthly Ordinances," "Jade Regalia," and "Mingtang" contain much Mingtang meaning; I therefore gather the two schools, compare them with the Monthly Ordinances, and take five Mingtang chambers as the universal rule past and present.
translations.idiomatic: "Monthly Ordinances," "Jade Regalia," and "Mingtang" contain much Mingtang doctrine; I gather the two schools, compare them with the Monthly Ordinances, and take five chambers as the rule for all ages.

sentences.zh: 其室居中者謂之太室，[4]太室之東者謂之青陽，當太室之南者謂之明堂，當太室之西者謂之總章，當太室之北者謂之玄堂；

translations.literal: The chamber in the center is called the Grand Chamber; [4] east of the Grand Chamber is called Green Yang; south of it, Bright Hall; west of it, Total Splendor; north of it, Dark Hall;
translations.idiomatic: The central chamber is the Grand Chamber; [4] east of it is Green Yang, south Bright Hall, west Total Splendor, north Dark Hall;

sentences.zh: 四面之室，各有夾房，謂之左右个，三十六戶七十二牖矣。

translations.literal: the chambers on the four sides each have side rooms called left and right "ge," thirty-six doors and seventy-two windows in all.
translations.idiomatic: each side chamber has flanking rooms called left and right ge—thirty-six doors and seventy-two windows in all.

sentences.zh: 室个之形，今之殿前，是其遺像耳。

translations.literal: The form of chambers and ge—the forecourt of today's halls—is their surviving image.
translations.idiomatic: The form of chamber and ge survives in the forecourt of today's halls.

sentences.zh: 个者，即寢之房也。

translations.literal: "Ge" is simply the side room of the sleeping hall.
translations.idiomatic: A ge is simply a side room of the sleeping hall.

sentences.zh: 但明堂與寢，施用既殊，故房、个之名亦隨事而遷耳。

translations.literal: Yet Mingtang and sleeping hall differ in use, so the names for rooms and ge also shift with the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Mingtang and sleeping hall differ in function, so the names for rooms and ge shift with the occasion.

sentences.zh: 今粗書其像，以見鄙意，案圖察義，略可驗矣。

translations.literal: Now I roughly sketch its form to show my humble opinion; examining the diagram and inspecting the meaning, it can in outline be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Here I sketch its form to show my view; inspect the diagram and the meaning can be tested in outline.

sentences.zh: 故檢之五室，則義明於考工；

translations.literal: Therefore checking the five chambers, the meaning is clear in the "Artificers";
translations.idiomatic: Check the five chambers and the meaning is clear in the "Artificers";

sentences.zh: 校之戶牖，則數協於盛德；

translations.literal: comparing doors and windows, the numbers agree with "Accomplished Virtue";
translations.idiomatic: compare doors and windows and the numbers agree with "Accomplished Virtue";

sentences.zh: 考之施用，則事著於月令；

translations.literal: examining application, the affairs appear in the Monthly Ordinances;
translations.idiomatic: examine use and the affairs appear in the Monthly Ordinances;

sentences.zh: 求之閏也，合周禮與玉藻。

translations.literal: seeking the intercalary month, it agrees with the Zhou Rites and "Jade Regalia."
translations.idiomatic: seek the intercalary month and it agrees with the Zhou Rites and "Jade Regalia."

sentences.zh: 既同夏殷，又符周秦，雖乖眾儒，儻或在斯矣。

translations.literal: It agrees with Xia and Yin and also matches Zhou and Qin; though it departs from the many Confucians, perhaps the truth lies here.
translations.idiomatic: It matches Xia and Yin and Zhou and Qin alike; though it offends many Confucians, perhaps truth lies here.

sentences.zh: 考工記曰：「周人明堂，度以九尺之筵，東西九筵，南北七筵，堂崇一筵。

translations.literal: The "Artificers" says: "The Zhou people's Mingtang is measured by the nine-foot mat; east and west nine mats, north and south seven mats, the hall one mat in height.
translations.idiomatic: The "Artificers" says, "The Zhou Mingtang is measured by the nine-foot mat: nine mats east and west, seven north and south, the hall one mat high.

sentences.zh: 五室，凡室二筵。

translations.literal: Five chambers—each chamber two mats in all.
translations.idiomatic: Five chambers—each chamber two mats.

sentences.zh: 室中度以几，堂上度以筵。」

translations.literal: Within chambers measure by the bench; in the hall measure by the mat."
translations.idiomatic: Within chambers measure by the bench; on the hall measure by the mat."

sentences.zh: 余謂記得之於五室，而謬於堂之修廣。

translations.literal: I hold that the record is right about the five chambers but wrong about the hall's length and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: I hold the record is right on five chambers but wrong on the hall's length and breadth.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 當以理推之，令愜古今之情也。

translations.literal: One should reason it out so as to satisfy the feelings of past and present.
translations.idiomatic: One must reason it out to satisfy the sense of past and present.

sentences.zh: 夫明堂者，蓋所以告月朔、布時令、宗文王、祀五帝者也。

translations.literal: The Mingtang is that by which one announces the new moon, promulgates the seasons, honors King Wen, and sacrifices to the Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: The Mingtang announces the new moon, promulgates seasons, honors King Wen, and sacrifices to the Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 然營構之範，自當因宜創制耳。

translations.literal: Yet the model for construction should naturally be created as circumstances require.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the model for building should be shaped to fit the need.

sentences.zh: 故五室者合於五帝各居一室之義。

translations.literal: Therefore five chambers accord with the meaning that the Five Emperors each dwell in one chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Five chambers fit the idea that each of the Five Emperors has his own chamber.

sentences.zh: 且四時之祀，皆據其方之正。

translations.literal: Moreover the seasonal sacrifices all take their proper direction.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal sacrifices each take their proper direction.

sentences.zh: 又聽朔布令，咸得其月之辰。

translations.literal: Again, hearing the new moon and promulgating orders all obtain the proper month and day.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the new moon and issuing orders each obtain the proper month and day.

sentences.zh: 可謂施政及祀，[5]二三俱允，求之古義，竊為當矣。

translations.literal: One may say government and sacrifice alike are satisfied; [5] both second and third are approved—sought in ancient meaning, I privately deem it correct.
translations.idiomatic: Government and sacrifice can both be served; [5] on both counts it holds—by ancient meaning, I believe it right.

sentences.zh: 鄭康成漢末之通儒，後學所宗正，釋五室之位，謂土居中，木火金水各居四維。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan, a comprehensive Confucian of late Han whom later students take as standard, explaining the position of the five chambers, says earth is centered and wood, fire, metal, and water each occupy the four corners.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan, late Han's comprehensive Confucian and later students' standard, places earth at the center and wood, fire, metal, and water in the four corners.

sentences.zh: 然四維之室既乖其正，施令聽朔各失厥衷。

translations.literal: Yet the corner chambers already depart from the proper directions, so promulgating orders and hearing the new moon each lose the center.
translations.idiomatic: Corner chambers miss the proper directions, so orders and new-moon rites each miss their center.

sentences.zh: 左右之个，棄而不顧，乃反文之以美說，飾之以巧辭，言水木用事交於東北，木火用事交於東南，火土用事交於西南，金水用事交於西北。

translations.literal: The left and right ge are abandoned and ignored; instead they ornament it with fine explanations and decorate it with clever phrases, saying water and wood meet in the northeast, wood and fire in the southeast, fire and earth in the southwest, metal and water in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right ge are ignored; instead clever phrases say water and wood meet in the northeast, wood and fire in the southeast, fire and earth in the southwest, metal and water in the northwest.

sentences.zh: 既依五行，當從其方，用事之交，[6]出何經典？

translations.literal: Since one relies on the Five Phases, one should follow their directions—where in the classics does the meeting of their dominion come from?
translations.idiomatic: If one follows the Five Phases, one should follow their directions—what classic authorizes these meetings of dominion?

sentences.zh: 可謂攻於異端，言非而博，疑誤後學，非所望於先儒也！

translations.literal: This may be called attacking heterodox paths, words wrong yet broad—misleading later students; it is not what one hopes for from former Confucians!
translations.idiomatic: This attacks heterodox paths with words wrong yet broad, misleading later students—not what one expects of former Confucians!

sentences.zh: 禮記玉藻曰，天子「聽朔於南門之外，閏月則闔門左扉，立於其中」。

translations.literal: The Record of Rites "Jade Regalia" says the Son of Heaven "hears the new moon outside the southern gate; in an intercalary month he closes the gate and stands at the left leaf, standing within it."
translations.idiomatic: "Jade Regalia" says the Son of Heaven "hears the new moon outside the southern gate; in an intercalary month he closes the gate, opens the left leaf, and stands within."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注曰：「天子之廟及路寢，皆如明堂制。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan annotates: "The Son of Heaven's ancestral temple and road sleeping hall are all like the Mingtang regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan notes, "The Son of Heaven's temple and road sleeping hall follow the Mingtang model.

sentences.zh: 明堂在國之陽，每月就其時之堂而聽朔焉。

translations.literal: The Mingtang is in the sunny side of the state; each month he goes to the hall of that season to hear the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The Mingtang stands on the state's sunny side; each month he goes to that season's hall to hear the new moon.

sentences.zh: 卒事，反宿路寢亦如之。

translations.literal: When the affair is finished he returns to lodge in the road sleeping hall as before.
translations.idiomatic: When finished he returns to lodge in the road sleeping hall as before.

sentences.zh: 閏月非常月，聽其朔於明堂門下，還處路寢門終月也。」

translations.literal: An intercalary month is not a regular month; he hears its new moon under the Mingtang gate and spends the month at the road sleeping hall gate."
translations.idiomatic: An intercalary month is irregular; he hears its new moon under the Mingtang gate and spends the month at the road sleeping hall gate."

sentences.zh: 而考工記「周人明堂」，玄注曰：「或舉王寢，或舉明堂，互言之以明其制同也。」

translations.literal: Yet in the "Artificers" "Zhou people's Mingtang," Xuan annotates: "Sometimes the king's sleeping hall is cited, sometimes the Mingtang—speaking alternately to show their regulations are the same."
translations.idiomatic: In "Zhou people's Mingtang" Xuan says, "Sometimes the king's sleeping hall is cited, sometimes the Mingtang—alternating to show one regulation."

sentences.zh: 其同制之言皆出鄭注。

translations.literal: All statements of sameness of regulation come from Zheng's commentary.
translations.idiomatic: All claims that the regulations are the same come from Zheng's commentary.

sentences.zh: 然則明堂與寢不得異矣。

translations.literal: In that case the Mingtang and sleeping hall cannot differ.
translations.idiomatic: Then Mingtang and sleeping hall cannot differ.

sentences.zh: 而尚書顧命篇曰：「迎子釗南門之外，延入翼室。」

translations.literal: Yet the "Charge to Zhong" in the Documents says: "Receive Prince Zhao outside the southern gate and lead him into the Wing Chamber."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Documents "Charge to Zhong" says, "Receive Prince Zhao outside the southern gate and lead him into the Wing Chamber."

sentences.zh: 此之翼室，即路寢矣。

translations.literal: This Wing Chamber is the road sleeping hall.
translations.idiomatic: That Wing Chamber is the road sleeping hall.

sentences.zh: 其下曰「大貝賁鼓在西房」，「垂之竹矢在東房」，此則路寢有左右房見於經史者也。

translations.literal: Below it says "great shells and decorated drums in the western room" and "bamboo arrows hanging in the eastern room"—here the road sleeping hall's left and right rooms appear in classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Below: "great shells and decorated drums in the western room," "bamboo arrows in the eastern room"—here left and right rooms of the road sleeping hall appear in classics.

sentences.zh: 禮記喪大記曰，「君夫人卒於路寢」，小斂，「婦人髽帶麻於房中」。

translations.literal: The Record of Rites "Greater Record of Mourning" says, "When the lord's wife dies in the road sleeping hall," at the lesser dressing, "the women bind their hair with hemp in the inner room."
translations.idiomatic: "Greater Record of Mourning" says, "When the lord's wife dies in the road sleeping hall," at lesser dressing, "women bind hair with hemp in the inner room."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注曰：「此蓋諸侯禮，帶麻於房中，則西房。」

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan annotates: "This is probably the rites of feudal lords; binding hemp in the inner room means the western room."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng notes, "This is probably feudal ritual; hemp in the inner room means the western room."

sentences.zh: [7]天子諸侯左右房見於注者也。

translations.literal: [7] The Son of Heaven and feudal lords' left and right rooms appear in commentary.
translations.idiomatic: [7] The Son of Heaven and feudal lords' left and right rooms appear in commentary.

sentences.zh: [8]論路寢則明其左右房，[9]言明堂則闕其左右个，同制之說還相矛盾，通儒之注，何其然乎？

translations.literal: [8] Discussing the road sleeping hall clarifies its left and right rooms; [9] speaking of the Mingtang omits its left and right ge—the theory of sameness of regulation is still contradictory. How can a comprehensive Confucian's commentary be so?
translations.idiomatic: [8] On the road sleeping hall he clarifies left and right rooms; [9] on the Mingtang he omits left and right ge—the sameness theory contradicts itself. How can a comprehensive Confucian's note be so?

sentences.zh: 使九室之徒奮筆而爭鋒者，豈不由處室之不當哉？

translations.literal: That the nine-chamber party brandish the brush and cross swords—is it not because the placement of chambers is wrong?
translations.idiomatic: That the nine-chamber school crosses swords—is it not because chamber placement is wrong?

sentences.zh: 記云：東西九筵，南北七筵，五室凡室二筵。

translations.literal: The record says: east and west nine mats, north and south seven mats, five chambers each two mats in all.
translations.idiomatic: The record says: nine mats east-west, seven north-south, five chambers of two mats each.

sentences.zh: 置五室於斯堂，雖使班、倕構思，王爾營度，則不能令三室不居其南北也。

translations.literal: Place five chambers in this hall—even if Ban and Yi thought, Wang Er planned—they could not keep three chambers from occupying north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Place five chambers in this hall—even Ban and Yi designing, Wang Er planning—three chambers must occupy north and south.

sentences.zh: 然則三室之間，便居六筵之地，而室壁之外裁有四尺五寸之堂焉。

translations.literal: Then between the three chambers one has six mats of space, while outside the chamber walls there is only a hall of four feet five inches.
translations.idiomatic: Between three chambers lie six mats; outside the walls the hall is only four feet five inches wide.

sentences.zh: 豈有天子布政施令之所，宗祀文王以配上帝之堂，周公負扆以朝諸侯之處，而室戶之外僅餘四尺而已哉？

translations.literal: Can there be a place where the Son of Heaven promulgates government and orders, sacrifices to King Wen to match the Lord on High, and the Duke of Zhou leans on the screen to receive the feudal lords—yet outside the chamber doors only four feet remain?
translations.idiomatic: Can the Son of Heaven's hall of government, sacrifice to King Wen to match Heaven, and Duke of Zhou's audience of feudal lords leave only four feet beyond the doors?

sentences.zh: 假在儉約，為陋過矣。

translations.literal: Even on the assumption of frugality, this would be excessively mean.
translations.idiomatic: Even in frugality this would be absurdly cramped.

sentences.zh: 論其堂宇則偏而非制，求之道理則未愜人情，其不然一也。

translations.literal: Speaking of its hall, it is skewed and not regulation; sought in reason, it does not satisfy human feeling—the first impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: Its hall is skewed, not regulation; in reason it fails human feeling—the first impossibility.

sentences.zh: 余恐為鄭學者，苟求必勝，競生異端以相訾抑。

translations.literal: I fear that followers of Zheng's learning, bent on victory, will compete in strange paths to pull one another down.
translations.idiomatic: I fear Zheng's followers, bent on winning, will invent strange arguments to pull one another down.

sentences.zh: 云二筵者，乃室之東西耳，南北則狹焉。

translations.literal: They say two mats are only east and west of the chamber; north and south are narrow.
translations.idiomatic: They say two mats are only east-west; north-south is narrow.

sentences.zh: 余故備論之曰：若東西二筵，則室戶之外為丈三尺五寸矣。

translations.literal: I therefore set out the full argument: if east and west are two mats, outside the chamber doors it is one zhang three feet five inches.
translations.idiomatic: I set out the argument: if east and west are two mats, outside the doors is one zhang three feet five inches.

sentences.zh: 南北戶外復如此，則三室之中南北裁各丈二尺耳。

translations.literal: North and south outside the doors are likewise, so within the three chambers north and south are only one zhang two feet each.
translations.idiomatic: North and south outside are the same; within three chambers north and south are only one zhang two feet each.

sentences.zh: 記云：「四旁兩夾窗。」

translations.literal: The record says: "On four sides, two flanking windows."
translations.idiomatic: The record says, "On four sides, two flanking windows."

sentences.zh: [10]若為三尺之戶，二尺之窗，窗戶之間，裁盈一尺。

translations.literal: [10] If doors are three feet and windows two feet, between window and door there is barely one foot.
translations.idiomatic: [10] If doors are three feet and windows two, barely a foot lies between them.

sentences.zh: 繩樞甕牖之室，蓽門圭竇之堂，尚不然矣。

translations.literal: A room with rope pivot and jar window, a hall with brushwood gate and pearl opening, would still not be so.
translations.idiomatic: A hovel with rope hinge and jar window, a hall with brushwood gate, would still not be so mean.

sentences.zh: 假令復欲小廣之，則四面之外闊狹不齊，東西既深，南北更淺，屋宇之制，不為通矣。

translations.literal: If one wished to enlarge it slightly, the outer breadth on four sides would be uneven—east and west already deep, north and south shallower—the building regulation would not be coherent.
translations.idiomatic: Enlarge it slightly and the outer breadths would be uneven—east-west deep, north-south shallow—the design would not cohere.

sentences.zh: 驗之眾塗，略無算焉。

translations.literal: Tested against many paths, there is scarcely any reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Tested many ways, it scarcely computes.

sentences.zh: 且凡室二筵，丈八地耳，然則戶牖之間不踰二尺也。

translations.literal: Moreover each chamber two mats is only one zhang eight of ground; then between door and window it does not exceed two feet.
translations.idiomatic: Two mats per chamber is only one zhang eight; door and window leave barely two feet between.

sentences.zh: 禮記明堂：「天子負斧扆南向而立。」

translations.literal: The Record of Rites "Mingtang": "The Son of Heaven, bearing the axe-screen, stands facing south."
translations.idiomatic: Record of Rites "Mingtang": "The Son of Heaven, bearing the axe-screen, faces south."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注曰：設斧於戶牖之間。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan annotates: set the axe between door and window.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng notes: set the axe between door and window.

sentences.zh: 而鄭氏禮圖說扆制曰：「縱廣八尺，畫斧文於其上，今之屏風也。」

translations.literal: Yet Zheng's ritual diagram on the screen says: "Length and breadth eight feet, axe pattern painted on it—today's folding screen."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's ritual diagram says, "Eight feet long and broad, axe pattern painted—today's folding screen."

sentences.zh: 以八尺扆置二尺之間，此之叵通，不待智者，較然可見矣。

translations.literal: Place an eight-foot screen in a two-foot space—this cannot cohere; without needing a wise man, comparison makes it plain.
translations.idiomatic: An eight-foot screen in two feet—incoherent; any man can see it.

sentences.zh: 且若二筵之室為四尺之戶，則戶之兩頰裁各七尺耳，全以置之，猶自不容，矧復戶牖之間哉？

translations.literal: Moreover if a two-mat chamber has a four-foot door, each cheek of the door is barely seven feet—even placing it whole there is no room, how much less between door and window?
translations.idiomatic: If a two-mat chamber has a four-foot door, each cheek is barely seven feet—no room even for the door, let alone door and window together.

sentences.zh: 其不然二也。

translations.literal: The second impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: The second impossibility.

sentences.zh: 又復以世代檢之，即虞夏尚朴，殷周稍文，制造之差，每加崇飾。

translations.literal: Again checking by generations: in Yu and Xia simplicity was still honored, in Yin and Zhou ornament increased; differences in manufacture grew more ornate each time.
translations.idiomatic: By generations: Yu and Xia prized simplicity, Yin and Zhou added ornament—each age grew more elaborate.

sentences.zh: 而夏后世室，堂修二七，周人之制，反更促狹，豈是夏禹卑宮之意，周監郁郁之美哉？

translations.literal: Yet the Xia dynasty's later chambers had halls seven by two mats, while the Zhou regulation is instead more cramped—how could this be Yu's intent of low palaces or Zhou's admiration of rich beauty?
translations.idiomatic: Xia's later chambers were seven by two mats; Zhou's rule is narrower—this is neither Yu's low palaces nor Zhou's rich beauty.

sentences.zh: 以斯察之，其不然三也。

translations.literal: Examined thus, the third impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: The third impossibility.

sentences.zh: 又云「堂崇一筵」，便基高九尺，而壁戶之外裁四尺五寸，於營制之法自不相稱。

translations.literal: It also says "the hall one mat in height," making the base nine feet high, while outside walls and doors there is only four feet five inches—in building law this is itself incompatible.
translations.idiomatic: "Hall one mat high" makes a nine-foot base, yet outside walls only four feet five—in building law this cannot match.

sentences.zh: 其不然四也。

translations.literal: The fourth impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth impossibility.

sentences.zh: 又云「室中度以几，堂上度以筵」，而復云「凡室二筵」，而不以几。

translations.literal: It also says "within chambers measure by the bench, in the hall measure by the mat," yet again says "each chamber two mats" and not by the bench.
translations.idiomatic: It says "chambers by bench, hall by mat," yet "each chamber two mats" not by bench.

sentences.zh: 還自相違，其不然五也。

translations.literal: It contradicts itself—the fifth impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: It contradicts itself—the fifth impossibility.

sentences.zh: 以此驗之，記者之謬，抑可見矣。

translations.literal: Verified thus, the error of the record can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the record's errors appear.

sentences.zh: 盛德篇云：[11]「明堂凡九室，三十六戶，七十二牖，上員下方，東西九仞，南北七筵，堂高三尺也。」

translations.literal: The "Accomplished Virtue" chapter says: [11] "The Mingtang has nine chambers in all, thirty-six doors, seventy-two windows, round above and square below, east and west nine ren, north and south seven mats, the hall three feet high."
translations.idiomatic: "Accomplished Virtue" says: [11] "The Mingtang has nine chambers, thirty-six doors, seventy-two windows, round above square below, nine ren east-west, seven mats north-south, hall three feet high."

sentences.zh: 余謂盛德篇得之於戶牖，失之於九室。

translations.literal: I hold that "Accomplished Virtue" is right about doors and windows but wrong about nine chambers.
translations.idiomatic: I hold "Accomplished Virtue" is right on doors and windows, wrong on nine chambers.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 五室之制，傍有夾房，面各有戶，戶有兩牖。

translations.literal: The regulation of five chambers has flanking rooms at the sides; each face has doors, each door two windows.
translations.idiomatic: Five chambers have flanking rooms; each face has doors, each door two windows.

sentences.zh: 此乃因事立則，非拘異術，戶牖之數，固自然矣。

translations.literal: This is establishing rules according to affairs, not binding oneself to strange arts—the number of doors and windows is naturally so.
translations.idiomatic: Rules arise from the affair itself, not from arbitrary artifice; the count of doors and windows follows naturally.

sentences.zh: 九室者，論之五帝，事既不合，施之時令，又失其辰。

translations.literal: Nine chambers, discussed in relation to the Five Emperors, do not fit the affair; applied to the seasonal ordinances, they again miss the proper days.
translations.idiomatic: Nine chambers, framed around the Five Emperors, fit neither the rites nor the seasonal calendar.

sentences.zh: 左右之个，重置一隅，兩辰同處，參差出入，斯乃義無所據，未足稱也。

translations.literal: The left and right ge are piled in one corner, two seasons in one place, uneven in and out—this has no basis in meaning and is not worth praise.
translations.idiomatic: Left and right ge crammed into one corner, two seasons sharing one site, rites uneven in and out—this has no proper basis and is not worth praising.

sentences.zh: 且又堂之修廣，裁六十三尺耳。

translations.literal: Moreover the hall's length and breadth is only sixty-three feet.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the hall measures only sixty-three feet in length and breadth.

sentences.zh: 假使四尺五寸為外之基，其中五十四尺便是五室之地。

translations.literal: Suppose four feet five inches as the outer foundation; within, fifty-four feet would be the ground of the five chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose the outer base is four feet five inches; within, fifty-four feet would be all the five chambers had.

sentences.zh: 計其一室之中，僅可一丈，置其戶牖，則於何容之哉？

translations.literal: Calculating within one chamber, barely one zhang—place doors and windows, and where could they be contained?
translations.idiomatic: Each chamber would be barely one zhang within—where could doors and windows even fit?

sentences.zh: 若必小而為之，以容其數，則令帝王側身出入，斯為怪矣。

translations.literal: If one must make them small to contain the numbers, it would make the Son of Heaven and emperors enter sideways—how strange!
translations.idiomatic: Shrink them to fit the numbers and emperors would have to sidle through—how absurd!

sentences.zh: 此匪直不合典制，抑亦可哂之甚也。

translations.literal: This is not only incompatible with canonical regulation; it is also supremely laughable.
translations.idiomatic: This fails canonical regulation and is frankly ridiculous.

sentences.zh: 余謂其九室之言，誠亦有由。

translations.literal: I hold that their talk of nine chambers indeed has some cause.
translations.idiomatic: Their talk of nine chambers does have some reason behind it.

sentences.zh: 然竊以為戴氏聞三十六戶、七十二牖，弗見其制，靡知所置，便謂一室有四戶之窗，計其戶牖之數，即以為九室耳。

translations.literal: Yet I privately think that the Dai clan heard of thirty-six doors and seventy-two windows, did not see the regulation, and did not know where to place them, and therefore supposed one chamber had four doors and windows; calculating the number of doors and windows, they took it to be nine chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I think the Dai clan heard of thirty-six doors and seventy-two windows, never saw the actual plan, and simply assumed four doors and windows per chamber—counting doors and windows, they called it nine chambers.

sentences.zh: 或未之思也。

translations.literal: Perhaps they did not think it through.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps they never thought it through.

sentences.zh: 蔡伯喈漢末之時學士，而見重於當時，即識其修廣之不當，而必未思其九室之為謬，更修而廣之，假其法像。

translations.literal: Cai Yong, a scholar of late Han valued in his time, already knew its length and breadth were wrong, yet surely did not reflect that nine chambers were wrong; he enlarged it further and borrowed its model.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong, a late Han scholar honored in his day, saw the dimensions were wrong yet never questioned nine chambers; he enlarged the design and borrowed its form.

sentences.zh: 可謂因偽飾辭，順非而澤，諒可歎矣。

translations.literal: This may be called dressing falsehood in fine words, glossing wrong as right—truly lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: This dresses falsehood in fine words and glosses error as truth—lamentable indeed.

sentences.zh: 余今省彼眾家，委心從善，庶探其衷，不為苟異。

translations.literal: Now I examine the many schools, commit my heart to what is good, hoping to probe their center and not differ for the sake of difference.
translations.idiomatic: Now I survey the schools, follow what is sound, and hope to find their center without differing for mere contrariness.

sentences.zh: 但是古非今，俗間之常情；

translations.literal: But to honor antiquity and reject the present is the common feeling of the vulgar;
translations.idiomatic: Honoring antiquity and rejecting the present is ordinary human prejudice;

sentences.zh: 愛遠惡近，世中之恒事。

translations.literal: loving the distant and disliking the near is the constant affair of the age.
translations.idiomatic: loving the far and disliking the near is the age's constant habit.

sentences.zh: 而千載之下，獨論古制，驚俗之談，固延多誚。

translations.literal: Yet a thousand years below, to discuss ancient regulations alone is talk that startles the vulgar and will naturally draw much ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand years on, to argue ancient regulations alone is talk that shocks the crowd and will draw ridicule.

sentences.zh: 脫有深賞君子者，覽而揣之，儻或存焉。

translations.literal: If there is a gentleman who deeply appreciates this, let him read and weigh it—perhaps something may remain.
translations.idiomatic: If some deeply discerning gentleman reads and weighs this, perhaps something may endure.

sentences.zh: 謐不飲酒，好音律，愛樂山水，高尚之情，長而彌固，一遇其賞，悠爾忘歸。

translations.literal: Mi did not drink wine, loved music, delighted in landscape; his lofty feeling grew firmer with years, and once he met what he prized he forgot to return.
translations.idiomatic: Mi did not drink, loved music and landscape; his lofty spirit grew firmer with age, and once he found what delighted him he forgot to return.

sentences.zh: 乃作神士賦，歌曰：「周孔重儒教，莊老貴無為。

translations.literal: He therefore composed the Rhapsody of the Divine Scholar, singing: "Zhou and Confucius honor Confucian teaching; Zhuangzi and Laozi prize non-action.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Rhapsody of the Divine Scholar, singing: "Zhou and Confucius honor Confucian teaching; Zhuangzi and Laozi prize non-action.

sentences.zh: 二途雖如異，一是買聲兒。

translations.literal: The two paths seem different, yet both are buying reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The two paths seem unlike, yet both are buying a name.

sentences.zh: 生乎意不愜，死名用何施。

translations.literal: If life does not satisfy the mind, what use is a name in death?
translations.idiomatic: If life does not satisfy the heart, what good is fame after death?

sentences.zh: 可心聊自樂，終不為人移。

translations.literal: What pleases the heart may briefly delight oneself; in the end one is not moved by others.
translations.idiomatic: What pleases the heart may briefly content oneself; in the end one is not swayed by others.

sentences.zh: 脫尋余志者，陶然正若斯。」

translations.literal: If one seeks my intent, one will be at ease just so."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever seeks my intent will find ease in just this."

sentences.zh: 延昌四年卒，年三十二，遐邇悼惜之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanchang he died at thirty-two; far and near mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanchang year 4 he died at thirty-two; mourners came from far and near.

sentences.zh: 其年，四門小學博士孔璠等學官四十五人上書曰：「竊見故處士趙郡李謐：十歲喪父，哀號罷隣人之相；

translations.literal: That year, Erudite of the Four Gates Elementary School Kong Fan and forty-five academic officers memorialized, saying: "We have observed the former recluse of Zhao commandery, Li Mi: at ten he lost his father, wailing until neighbors ceased mutual condolence;
translations.idiomatic: That year Kong Fan, Erudite of the Four Gates Elementary School, and forty-five academic officers memorialized: "We observe the former recluse Li Mi of Zhao: at ten he lost his father and wailed until neighbors ceased condoling one another;

sentences.zh: 幼事兄瑒，恭順盡友于之誠。

translations.literal: in youth he served his elder brother Yang with respectful obedience, fully displaying the sincerity of brotherly friendship.
translations.idiomatic: in youth he served his elder brother Yang with full brotherly devotion.

sentences.zh: 十三通孝經、論語、毛詩、尚書，歷數之術尤盡其長，州閭鄉黨有神童之號。

translations.literal: At thirteen he mastered the Classic of Filial Piety, Analects, Mao Odes, and Documents; especially in calendrical arts he exhausted his strength—throughout district and village he had the title of divine child.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he mastered the Filial Piety Classic, Analects, Mao Odes, and Documents; in calendrical arts he excelled—district and village called him a divine child.

sentences.zh: 年十八，詣學受業，時博士即孔璠也。

translations.literal: At eighteen he went to study and receive instruction; the erudite at the time was Kong Fan himself.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he came to study; the erudite then was Kong Fan himself.

sentences.zh: 覽始要終，論端究緒，授者無不欣其言矣。

translations.literal: From beginning to end he surveyed and pursued the thread; those who received his teaching were all delighted by his words.
translations.idiomatic: From first to last he traced every thread; all who heard him were delighted.

sentences.zh: 於是鳩集諸經，廣校同異，比三傳事例，名春秋叢林，十有二卷。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gathered the classics, broadly collated agreements and differences, compared the examples of the Three Commentaries, and named it Thicket of the Spring and Autumn—twelve scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the classics, collated agreements and differences, compared the Three Commentaries, and compiled the Thicket of the Spring and Autumn in twelve scrolls.

sentences.zh: 為璠等判析隱伏，垂盈百條。

translations.literal: For Fan and others he judged hidden points, more than a hundred items in all.
translations.idiomatic: For Fan and others he resolved hidden difficulties—more than a hundred items.

sentences.zh: 滯無常滯，纖毫必舉；

translations.literal: Where stagnation had no constant stagnation, the slightest thread was raised;
translations.idiomatic: Where confusion had no fixed form, he raised the slightest point;

sentences.zh: 通不長通，有枉斯屈。

translations.literal: where penetration did not long penetrate, if there was wrong he bent it.
translations.idiomatic: where insight faltered, if there was error he corrected it.

sentences.zh: 不苟言以違經，弗飾辭而背理。

translations.literal: He did not speak carelessly against the classics, nor ornament words against reason.
translations.idiomatic: He would not speak carelessly against the classics or ornament words against reason.

sentences.zh: 辭氣磊落，觀者忘疲。

translations.literal: His words were bold and open; viewers forgot fatigue.
translations.idiomatic: His manner was bold and open; listeners forgot fatigue.

sentences.zh: 每曰：『丈夫擁書萬卷，何假南面百城。』

translations.literal: He often said: "A man with ten thousand scrolls—why need he face south over a hundred cities?"
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "A man with ten thousand scrolls—why need a hundred cities facing south?"

sentences.zh: 遂絕跡下幃，杜門却掃，棄產營書，手自刪削，卷無重複者四千有餘矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he cut off his tracks below the curtain, shut the door and swept the courtyard, abandoned property to build books, personally edited and pruned—more than four thousand scrolls without duplication.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew behind his curtain, shut his door, sold property for books, and personally edited more than four thousand scrolls without duplication.

sentences.zh: 猶括次專家，搜比讜議，隆冬達曙，盛暑通宵。

translations.literal: Still he indexed specialists and searched comparative commentaries—deep winter until dawn, midsummer through the night.
translations.idiomatic: He still indexed specialists and compared commentaries—working from deep winter to dawn and through midsummer nights.

sentences.zh: 雖仲舒不闚園，君伯之閉戶，高氏之遺漂，張生之忘食，方之斯人，未足為喻。

translations.literal: Though Dong Zhongshu did not peep into the garden, Cui Yuan shut his door, Gao's legacy drifted away, and Master Zhang forgot food—compared with this man, they are not enough for a likeness.
translations.idiomatic: Though Dong Zhongshu never glanced into his garden, Cui Yuan shut his door, Gao drifted on the river, and Zhang forgot to eat—none equals this man.

sentences.zh: 謐嘗詣故太常卿劉芳推問音義，語及中代興廢之由，芳乃歎曰：『君若遇高祖，侍中、太常非僕有也。』

translations.literal: Mi once visited the former Minister of Ceremonies Liu Fang to inquire about sounds and meanings; speaking of the rise and fall of the middle age, Fang sighed and said: "If you had met Emperor Gaozu, Secretariat Director and Minister of Ceremonies would not have been mine."
translations.idiomatic: Mi once visited former Minister of Ceremonies Liu Fang on sounds and meanings; speaking of dynastic rise and fall, Fang sighed: "Had you met Gaozu, Secretariat Director and Minister of Ceremonies would not have been mine."

sentences.zh: 前河南尹、黃門侍郎甄琛內贊近機，朝野傾目，于時親識求官者，答云：『趙郡李謐，耽學守道，不悶于時，常欲致言，但未有次耳。

translations.literal: The former Henan Intendant and Palace Attendant Zhen Chen inwardly assisted near policy; court and countryside turned their eyes. When acquaintances then sought office, he answered: "Li Mi of Zhao commandery is absorbed in learning and keeps the Way, not troubled by the age—I have often wished to speak for him but have not yet had the chance.
translations.idiomatic: Former Henan Intendant and Palace Attendant Zhen Chen held power at court; when friends sought office he answered: "Li Mi of Zhao is absorbed in learning and keeps the Way, untroubled by the age—I have long meant to speak for him but lacked the chance.

sentences.zh: 諸君何為輕自媒衒？』

translations.literal: Why do you gentlemen lightly advertise yourselves?"
translations.idiomatic: Why do you lightly peddle yourselves?"

sentences.zh: 謂其子曰：『昔鄭玄、盧植不遠數千里詣扶風馬融，今汝明師甚邇，何不就業也？』

translations.literal: He told his son: "In the past Zheng Xuan and Lu Zhi traveled thousands of li to Fufeng to study with Ma Rong; now your bright teacher is very near—why not take instruction?"
translations.idiomatic: He told his son, "Zheng Xuan and Lu Zhi once traveled thousands of li to study with Ma Rong in Fufeng; your teacher is near—why not study?"

sentences.zh: 又謂朝士曰：『甄琛行不媿時，但未薦李謐，以此負朝廷耳。』

translations.literal: He also told court gentlemen: "Zhen Chen's conduct does not shame the age, but only that he did not recommend Li Mi—by this he failed the court."
translations.idiomatic: He told court gentlemen, "Zhen Chen's conduct shames no one, but he failed the court by not recommending Li Mi."

sentences.zh: 又結宇依巖，憑崖鑿室，方欲訓彼青衿，宣揚墳典，冀西河之教重興、北海之風不墜。

translations.literal: He also built a dwelling against the cliff, carved rooms in the rock, intending to instruct the blue-collared youths, spread the classics of the tombs, hoping to revive the teaching of Xihe and keep the wind of Beihai from falling.
translations.idiomatic: He built cliff dwellings and carved rock rooms, intending to teach young scholars and spread the classics, hoping to revive Xihe's teaching and keep Beihai's wind alive.

sentences.zh: 而祐善空聞，暴疾而卒。

translations.literal: Yet Heaven's favor was heard only in vain; he died suddenly of a violent illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven's favor rang hollow; he died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 邦國銜殄悴之哀，儒生結摧梁之慕。

translations.literal: The state bore the grief of ruin and withering; Confucian students bound the sorrow of a broken beam.
translations.idiomatic: The realm mourned a broken pillar; scholars mourned a fallen beam.

sentences.zh: 況璠等或服議下風，或親承音旨，師儒之義，其可默乎！」

translations.literal: How much more Fan and others, some submitting to his arguments, some personally receiving his instruction—the duty of teacher and student—how could they be silent!"
translations.idiomatic: How much more Fan and others, some submitting to his teaching, some hearing him in person—how could teacher and student stay silent!"

sentences.zh: 事奏，詔曰：「謐屢辭徵辟，志守沖素，儒隱之操，深可嘉美。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict said: "Mi repeatedly declined summons and commissions, his will guarding pure simplicity—recluse-Confucian conduct deeply praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached the throne; the edict said, "Mi repeatedly declined summons; his will guards pure simplicity—recluse conduct deeply praiseworthy.

sentences.zh: 可遠傍惠、康，近準玄晏，諡曰貞靜處士，并表其門閭，以旌高節。」

translations.literal: He may be compared at a distance to Hui and Kang, at hand to Xuan Yan; posthumous title Recluse of Upright Stillness, and his gate and lane are to be marked to honor his lofty integrity."
translations.idiomatic: Compare him from afar to Hui and Kang, near at hand to Xuan Yan; grant the posthumous title Recluse of Upright Stillness and mark his gate and lane to honor his integrity."

sentences.zh: 遣謁者奉冊，於是表其門曰文德，里曰孝義云。

translations.literal: A messenger was sent with the patent; thereupon his gate was marked Literary Virtue and his lane Filial Duty."
translations.idiomatic: A messenger bore the patent; his gate was marked Literary Virtue and his lane Filial Duty.

sentences.zh: 鄭脩，北海人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xiu was a man of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xiu came from Beihai.

sentences.zh: 少隱於岐南几谷中，依巖結宇，獨處淡然，屏迹人事，不交世俗，耕食水飲，皮冠草服，雅好經史，專意玄門。

translations.literal: In youth he retired to Jigu Valley south of Qi, built a dwelling against the cliff, dwelt alone with calm detachment, screened his tracks from human affairs, did not mingle with the vulgar, plowed for food and drank water, wore bark crown and grass clothes, elegantly loved classics and histories, and devoted himself to the dark gate.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he retired to Jigu Valley south of Qi, built cliff dwellings, lived alone in calm detachment, shunned worldly affairs, plowed and drank water, wore bark crown and grass robes, loved the classics, and devoted himself to the Way.

sentences.zh: 前後州將，每徵不至。

translations.literal: Provincial governors before and after repeatedly summoned him, but he never came.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial governors repeatedly summoned him; he never came.

sentences.zh: 岐州刺史魏蘭根頻遣致命，脩不得已，暫出見蘭根，尋還山舍。

translations.literal: Wei Langen, Inspector of Qi, repeatedly sent urgent messages; Xiu, unable to refuse further, briefly came out to see Langen and soon returned to his mountain dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Langen, Inspector of Qi, sent repeated summons; Xiu, unable to refuse, briefly met him and soon returned to the hills.

sentences.zh: 蘭根申表薦脩，肅宗詔付雍州刺史蕭寶夤訪實以聞。

translations.literal: Langen submitted a memorial recommending Xiu; Emperor Suzong ordered Yongzhou Inspector Xiao Baoyin to investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: Langen memorialized recommending Xiu; Emperor Suzong ordered Yongzhou Inspector Xiao Baoyin to investigate and report.

sentences.zh: 會寶夤作逆，事不行。

translations.literal: When Baoyin rebelled, the affair did not go through.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin rebelled, the matter came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：古之所謂隱逸者，非伏其身而不見也，非閉其言而不出也，非藏其智而不發也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: What antiquity called recluses is not hiding the body so it is not seen, not closing words so they do not come forth, not concealing wisdom so it is not released.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Antiquity's recluses did not hide the body unseen, seal words unspoken, or bury wisdom unused.

sentences.zh: 蓋以恬淡為心，不曒不昧，安時處順，與物無私者也。

translations.literal: Rather, with calm detachment as heart, neither bright nor dim, accommodating the time and settling in accord, without private feeling toward things.
translations.idiomatic: They took calm detachment as heart, neither glaring nor dim, settled with the age, and held no private grudge against things.

sentences.zh: 眭夸輩忘懷纓冕，畢志丘園。

translations.literal: Sui Kua and his kind forgot official regalia and fulfilled their will in gardens and fields.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Kua and his kind forgot rank and fulfilled their will in garden and field.

sentences.zh: 或隱不違親，貞不絕俗；

translations.literal: Some retired without violating kin, chaste without cutting off the vulgar;
translations.idiomatic: Some withdrew without failing kin, remained pure without severing the world;

sentences.zh: 或不教而勸，虛往實歸。

translations.literal: some taught without lecturing, empty in going, full in returning.
translations.idiomatic: some taught without preaching—empty in departure, full in return.

sentences.zh: 非有自然純德，其孰能至於此哉？

translations.literal: Without natural pure virtue, who could reach this?
translations.idiomatic: Without innate pure virtue, who could reach this?
